findings.where: below the fold of the US region: the report lists five modules — dates, todos, calendar, rituals, shelf — and the artifact shows only the first three (DATES / next: the place by the bridge, TO DO / 10 open, DATES THAT MATTER / us in 63 days)
findings.what: The rituals surface, the one place in the product where a streak count, a 'days in a row', or a broken-streak warning would live, appears in no artifact in evidence/ — not in 03_us.png, not in any frame I stepped through of 06, 07, 08, 11 or 15 — and the shelf surface likewise; the only rituals evidence is the glance string 'last: tuesday soup' and one chat note reading 'text when home | KEPT' in 02_chat.png at y1434-1605.
findings.why: The row asks for no engagement machinery of any kind anywhere in the build, and the surface most likely to carry it was never photographed, so compliance there is asserted rather than shown; what can be seen (a KEPT stamp with a single tally stroke and no number, a glance that names the last ritual rather than a run length) is clean, which is why this is serious rather than blocking.

findings.what: The sweep that would otherwise carry the voice anti-goal cannot be taken at face value on two counts I can check against the file: its rule 'an exclamation mark' has pattern '!' yet the read set contains a string with a literal '!' in it (calendar_module.dart:157, '${m.yearsAt(next!)} years') and findings is empty, so that rule does not fire as written; and at least five strings the app demonstrably displays are absent from the read set — the module glances 'next: the place by the bridge', '10 open', 'us in 63 days', 'last: tuesday soup' and 'waiting on you: the one you said you stopped' (evidence/logs/03_us.report.json), three of which are legible in 03_us.png.
findings.why: The row is scored on every string the app displays, and '0 findings over 115 strings' is corroboration rather than coverage; the strings themselves read clean, so this costs little, but the pixels rather than the log are what carry the row.

findings.where: the feeling row of 01_pulse at y1170-1510 ('hold', a plain grey cylinder); 08 sampled frames 12-17 ('here', a grey open box; 'a squeeze', a pinched grey slab); 11 sampled frames 0-1 ('thinking of you', two grey slabs; 'goodnight', a grey card with a white folded corner)
findings.what: Six of the feeling objects render as near-neutral grey geometric forms whose identity is not readable without the caption printed under them — measured on 01_pulse.png the 'hold' cylinder body sits at mean saturation 0.120 and the 'goodnight' card face at 0.106, against the desk's 0.31 — so the word, not the object, is doing the work.
findings.why: The row forbids stock illustration standing in for feeling; these are bespoke rendered objects rather than clip art and so are not a violation, but a generic untextured primitive under a caption is the nearest thing in the build to a stand-in, and it is the direction the anti-goal warns against.

what_is_working: No emoji, anywhere, by measurement: in eight of the ten stills exactly zero pixels exceed HSV saturation 0.55; 01_pulse.png has 887 such pixels and every one of them is the dark navy pen ink of the 'ugh' scribble (mean RGB 20,26,46, all inside x336-572 / y1264-1955) and 14_media_viewer.png has 94, inside the photograph. A single colour emoji glyph at 1440x3120 would put thousands of saturated pixels on screen.

The feeling vocabulary is a coherent desk world rather than a symbol set: surfaces.json names 34 objects — crane, fortune teller, spitball, staple chain, dog ear, torn corner, coffee ring, rubber band, snapped pencil, plaster, wrapper — plus four drawn in the app with a pen (chair, scribble, thumbprint, window). haptics_strip.png lists all 36 feelings by name and every one is a plain lowercase phrase: 'a squeeze', 'i'll make you tea', 'long day', 'not okay', 'tuesday soup', 'stuck with me'.

The voice holds across every string I could read in ten stills and 76 sampled clip frames: no exclamation mark, no 'Oops', no 'get started', no 'you're all set', the reader is never a user, and the app never names itself — the PWA manifest name is 'the other phone' (evidence/logs/pwa.json). Setup reads 'put this phone on the tailnet' and 'read the six words off the other phone'; failure reads 'it would not go' and 'can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.'

The notification surface in 05_settings.png is the inverse of engagement machinery: 'let it interrupt you' with quiet hours 23:00 to 07:00 and a per-kind three-way choice of wake me / quietly / not at all, with five of nine kinds already set below 'wake me'. The push payload itself carries no copy and no badge count — evidence/logs/webpush.txt shows the recovered plaintext is {"kind":"feeling","from":"noor"}, 32 bytes, keys ['kind','from'] only.

No counter in any artifact accumulates or rewards. '10 open' is a todo count, 'us in 63 days' a calendar distance, '72%' a partner battery, '41s'/'21s'/'63s' in 04_moments.png are clip durations, and the ritual instance in 02_chat.png is stamped 'KEPT' beside a single hand-drawn tally stroke with no number attached.

The paper is photographic, not simulated, and it measures that way. At 300% (02_chat_300_edge.png) individual fibres cross the paper/desk boundary. Blank paper patches in 02_chat.png, 01_pulse.png and 13_messenger_states.png carry high-pass detail of 5.2-7.6 grey levels with lag-1 autocorrelation 0.82-0.99 across and 0.69-0.85 down — structured and anisotropic, where a procedural noise overlay would sit near zero. surfaces.json measures 54 distinct paper stocks, none flat (lowest patch_std 2.29 against a floor of 1.2), and tears.json reports 9 visible notes with 9 distinct tear profiles and no repeats out of a pool of 56.

Nothing is tiled. On 10_first_run.png, which is almost all bare desk, the best 2D normalised cross-correlation between the frame and itself is 0.35 over horizontal offsets from 240 to 720 px and 0.44 over vertical offsets from 100 to 1560 px; a repeating tile would return a value near 1.0 at its period, and none appears.

Nothing is a rounded rectangle. Measured on the CHAT tab in 02_chat.png, the left edge goes from inset to full extent inside a single scanline (row 10 to row 11 of the crop at x300-580, y2950), i.e. a square corner with a radius under about 1 px at capture resolution; the tabs and the search chip are straight-cut paper carrying grain and blue ruled lines rather than a flat beige fill.
verdict: I went looking for all four forbidden interpretations and found none of them on screen. There is no emoji anywhere — eight of ten stills contain literally zero pixels above 0.55 saturation, and the two exceptions are pen ink and a photograph. The feeling layer is a vocabulary of thirty-four paper and stationery objects with thirty-six plain lowercase names, which is the opposite of emoji soup and the opposite of stock art. The voice is uniform and unmarketed across every string I could read in ten stills and seventy-six sampled clip frames: no exclamation mark, no cheer, no user, no self-naming, and the app calls itself 'the other phone' in its own manifest. And the paper survives measurement rather than merely looking right at a glance — fibres cross the torn edge at 300%, blank stock carries structured anisotropic grain instead of white noise, fifty-four distinct stocks are measured with none flat, nine visible tears are nine distinct profiles, no offset in either axis produces a tiling correlation above 0.44, and the nav tabs turn their corners inside one scanline. What keeps this from full marks is not something present but something absent: the US region is five modules and only three of them reach an artifact. Rituals — the module the mission goal itself pairs with the word streaks — is visible nowhere in evidence/, and the build's own string sweep applies its streak rule only to files whose path contains 'ritual' and read exactly one line from that path, the empty state. Everything I can see of rituals is clean, a KEPT stamp with a tally stroke and no number and a glance that names the last one kept rather than a run length, and that is why this sits well above the floor rather than at it; but a populated rituals view was never photographed, and that is the one place an unseen counter could still be hiding. One thing outside this row that a reader should know I noticed and deliberately did not charge here: the desk under the paper is a drawn wood, soft vertical bands with no pore structure, carrying 11.1% high-pass detail against the paper's 1.7% — it is not paper and so not this row's business, but it is the least material-true surface in the build and belongs to whoever scores material truth.
